messages:
maya.k: heads up — found a weird formatting regression after we rolled gptx-7b-awq-int8 to the onboarding canary. JSON/CSV outputs are getting extra/backslash escapes and sometimes truncated brackets. repro below.

sam.p: ugh. which eval suite and how big is the delta? link?

maya.k: quick numbers from the canary run (json-schema prompt set): EM(drop) ~6.4% absolute, ROUGE-L -2.1, hallucination_count x3 on code/json tasks. full eval: https://internal.redwood/evals/2145006789 (canary id).

raj: do we know if this is AWQ-specific or if GPTQ/FP8 also shows it? could be a kernel/codepath that mishandles quote tokens after quantization.

maya.k: repro across AWQ-int8 and GPTQ with our compressed kernels, but fp16/fp8 baseline not showing the escape duplication. baseline fp16 -> correct: {\"name\": \"O'Reilly\"} ; awq-int8 -> \"{\\\"name\\\": \\\"O\\'Reilly\\\"}\" (notice double wrapping / extra escaping).

aisha: please paste a raw example from model stdout (no postprocessing). also try short vs long prefix — kv boundary bugs have popped up before.

maya.k: raw snippet from canary stdout: ```
{\"id\":123, \"payload\": \"{\\\"name\\\": \\\"O\\'Reilly\\\"}\"}
```

leo: that looks like the tokenizer or the postprocess escaping layer is applied twice. but why only after quant? runtime might be substituting a different text-output codepath. check compile flags for text-escape optimization.

raj: I'm suspicious of prefix-length dependent batching. can you run the same prompt with fixed-seq-len 256 and 1024 and compare? sometimes awq block packing triggers an alternate emitter.

maya.k: running now. cmd I'm using: ```bash
python -m rdinfer.eval --model gptx-7b --quant awq-int8 --prompt-set json-keys --seq-len 256 --dump-raw stdout_sample.txt
```

deploy-bot: Canary rollout updated: gptx-7b-awq-int8 -> traffic 5% -> 2% (manual throttle by ops).

sam.p: good call on short/long. also request an eval that isolates only postprocessing: return raw token ids and detokenize with our reference tokenizer to confirm whether problem is model output or detokenizer.

aisha: try alternate quant params: awq with blocksize 64, awq with per-channel options, and a GPTQ run for comparison. if GPTQ passes then AWQ-specific. also include FP8 run to be safe.

maya.k: results so far: seq-len 256 -> still bad; seq-len 1024 -> output truncated in some cases (missing trailing '}'). AWQ blocksize=64 reduces double-escape but doesn't eliminate it. gptq-int8 run shows only minor escapes (EM drop 1.1%). fp16 shows no issue.

leo: compile/kernel differences between AWQ and GPTQ likely. pinging eng-runtime to check text-emitter commit. @raj can you grab kernel compile logs from the canary nodes?

raj: grabbing logs now. also found one suspicious env flag on the canary image: TEXT_EMIT_COMPACT=true (not set on baseline). looks like that toggles a different escape routine.

maya.k: confirmed flipping TEXT_EMIT_COMPACT=false on a test node fixes escaping. but we still see occasional truncation on longer sequences.

sam.p: plan: 1) revert canary routing to fp16 fallback for production traffic 2) disable TEXT_EMIT_COMPACT in canary until we root-cause 3) run targeted bisect across AWQ params and kernel commits 4) create a small eval harness that returns raw token ids + reference detok.

aisha: I'll start the AWQ param sweep and baseline GPTQ/FP8 runs. putting results into this eval run: https://internal.redwood/evals/2145006789/compare (will push CSV).

evalbot: eval run queued: id 2145006799. will post artifacts when done.

leo: thanks — also add a short prompt set for CSV quoting and latex delimiters (we saw math-mode delimiters break in a separate ticket last month). good to catch early.

maya.k: created issue #INF-3127 with initial repro + raw logs and attached stdout_sample.txt. assigning to eng-runtime and eng-ml.

raj: noting: this looks high priority given downstream customers hitting malformed JSON. I'll schedule a 15m sync after evalbot posts results.

sam.p: :thumbsup: keep short-lived canary routing and avoid full rollout until we confirm root.

maya.k: thanks all — will post updated artifacts and the token-id traces from both awq and gptq once eval finishes.

leo: acknowledged.
